name: AutoSleep
description: Put idle Heroku apps to sleep and wake them on the next request. A self-hosted, open-source alternative to AutoIdle.

API_USER.description: Username for the AutoSleep dashboard and API (HTTP basic auth).

API_PASS.description: Password for the AutoSleep dashboard and API. Generated for you; see it later with `heroku config:get API_PASS`.

PASSPHRASE.description: Encrypts stored Heroku tokens. Don't change it after setup, or stored tokens become unreadable.

HEROKU_API_KEY.description: Recommended. A Heroku API key so AutoSleep can see and manage your apps. Create one with `heroku authorizations:create -d autosleep` and paste the Token. You can also add it later in the dashboard.

HEROKU_OAUTH_ID.description: Optional. OAuth client ID so you can connect your Heroku account with one click (create one at https://dashboard.heroku.com/account/applications with callback URL https://<this-app>.herokuapp.com/auth/heroku/callback). Leave empty to use API keys instead.

HEROKU_OAUTH_SECRET.description: Optional. OAuth client secret matching HEROKU_OAUTH_ID.

ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL.description: Optional. A Slack or Discord incoming-webhook URL. AutoSleep posts failed sleeps/wakes there, and a savings digest every Monday.

USERS.description: Optional. More logins for your team, comma separated name:password:role, where role is admin or viewer (read-only). Example: alice:s3cret:admin,qa:hunter2:viewer

WHITELISTED_IPS.description: Optional. Comma-separated CIDRs allowed to use the dashboard/API, e.g. 203.0.113.0/24. Empty allows any IP (basic auth still required).

NIGHT_MODE_TZ.description: Time zone for the night-mode window (IANA name, e.g. Asia/Kolkata, Europe/Berlin).

NIGHT_MODE_START.description: When the night-mode window starts, HH:MM in NIGHT_MODE_TZ.

NIGHT_MODE_HOURS.description: How long the night-mode window lasts, in hours.
